name: Floodplain forest
notes: Riparian bottomland forest of fast-growing cottonwoods, willows, sycamore and silver maple that tolerate seasonal flooding, over cane, dogwood and tall nettle/fern ground cover threaded with vines; drawn on the Mississippi/Missouri bottoms and the Rhine/Danube floodplains.

canopy.name: Cottonwood
canopy.source: Populus deltoides, eastern cottonwood, central & eastern North America, pioneer of river floodplains and sandbars, 25-40 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

canopy.name: Sycamore
canopy.source: Platanus occidentalis, American sycamore, eastern North America, bottomland and riverbank forest, 25-40 m mottled white bark — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

canopy.name: Silver maple
canopy.source: Acer saccharinum, silver maple, eastern North America, flood-tolerant floodplain forest and stream banks, 20-30 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

canopy.name: White willow
canopy.source: Salix alba, white willow, Europe to Central Asia, softwood floodplain forest along large rivers, 15-25 m silvery leaves — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

canopy.name: Black poplar
canopy.source: Populus nigra, black poplar, Europe to W Asia, riverine floodplain woodland on gravel and sand, 20-30 m — Wikipedia / EUFORGEN

canopy.name: Pecan
canopy.source: Carya illinoinensis, pecan, Mississippi valley to Mexico, bottomland hardwood forest on rich alluvium, 25-40 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Giant river cane
shrub.source: Arundinaria gigantea, giant river cane, southeastern USA, dense canebrakes on floodplains, 2-8 m native bamboo — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Red-osier dogwood
shrub.source: Cornus sericea, red-osier dogwood, northern & western North America, thickets on stream banks and floodplains, 1.5-4 m red stems — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Grey willow
shrub.source: Salix cinerea, grey willow, Europe & W Asia, willow carr on floodplains and wet ground, 3-8 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

shrub.name: Elderberry
shrub.source: Sambucus nigra, elder, Europe & W Asia, nutrient-rich riverside woodland and levees, 3-6 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Stinging nettle
ground.source: Urtica dioica, stinging nettle, Eurasia & North America, dominant tall herb on nitrogen-rich floodplain soils, 0.5-1.5 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Reed canary grass
ground.source: Phalaris arundinacea, reed canary grass, circumboreal, wet floodplain margins and ditches, 0.6-2 m — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

ground.name: Ostrich fern
ground.source: Matteuccia struthiopteris, ostrich fern, circumboreal, colonies on shaded river floodplains, vase of fronds 1-1.7 m — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

ground.name: Jewelweed
ground.source: Impatiens capensis, orange jewelweed, eastern North America, dense stands on wet shaded floodplain ground, 0.5-1.5 m orange flowers — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Sedge
ground.source: Carex grayi, Gray's sedge, eastern North America, floodplain forest floor and swampy woods, 40-90 cm, spiky mace-like heads — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Riverbank grape
epiphyte.source: Vitis riparia, riverbank grape, central & eastern North America, drapes floodplain trees to 25 m, dark purple fruit — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Virginia creeper
epiphyte.source: Parthenocissus quinquefolia, Virginia creeper, eastern North America to Mexico, climbs trunks in bottomland forest to 20 m, scarlet autumn — USDA Plants / Wikipedia
